categories.title: Probabilistic logic programs

groups.title: Paths in random graphs
groups.about: A random directed graph of n nodes and m probabilistic edges: the probability of a path from node 1 to each node, by size.

groups.title: Paths in grids
groups.about: An n by n grid of probabilistic right and down edges (and some left and up): the probability of a path from one corner to the other, by n.

groups.title: Biomine's paths
groups.about: The union of the K most probable paths between Alzheimer disease and four genes in Biomine, a network of biological entities with probabilistic links: the probability that each gene is connected to the disease, by K.
groups.source: ProbLog's first workload (De Raedt et al., IJCAI 2007) on Biomine's human graph of 2018

groups.title: Smokers
groups.about: The smokers network of n people, each with a few friends, by n.

groups.title: Symmetric smokers
groups.about: The smokers network of n people whose friendships are mutual, each pair of friends linked both ways, by n; each size is the one before with more people and their friendships.

groups.title: UW-CSE
groups.about: The UW-CSE CP-logic theory with one course, one professor and n students: annotated disjunctions and negation, by n.

groups.title: Cora's citation matching
groups.about: Citation matching on Cora (fold m1, 1493 facts) under the initial theory of its learning problem: the probability of q samebib queries, by q.

groups.title: Blood type
groups.about: cplint's Mendelian blood type example.

groups.title: Pedigrees
groups.about: cplint's blood type rules on a loopy pedigree of g generations of w people, a third of the blood types before the last generation observed: the last generation's blood types, by g and w.
groups.source: Meert et al. (ILP 2009); Riguzzi and Swift (TPLP 2011), written by gen_pedigree.py

groups.title: Sickness
groups.about: n people on a power-law friendship graph over t steps, cyclic within a step and chained across steps, a third of the earlier sick atoms observed: who is sick at the last step, by n and t.
groups.source: Vlasselaer et al. (IJAR 2016, Example 10), written by gen_sickness.py

groups.title: Mastermind
groups.about: The game of Mastermind with p pegs in c colours, the black and white pegs of r random guesses observed: every peg's colour, by c, p and r.
groups.source: Chavira, Darwiche and Jaeger (IJAR 2006) as the program of Vlasselaer et al. (IJAR 2016), written by gen_mastermind.py

groups.title: MNIST addition
groups.about: DeepProbLog's addition task grown to n digits, each a ten-valued annotated disjunction, the sum built by partial sums: every value of the sum, by n.
groups.source: Manhaeve et al. (NeurIPS 2018), grown as in Scallop (Li et al., PLDI 2023), written by gen_mnist_sum.py

groups.title: Event calculus
groups.about: Prob-EC's event definitions over a simulated scene of 4 people in T frames, each frame's short-term activities probabilistic: the long-term activities meeting and moving of every pair every 10th frame, by T.
groups.source: Skarlatidis et al. (TPLP 2015), written by gen_eventcalc.py

groups.title: Taint analysis of Android apps
groups.about: A points-to and taint analysis of 104 probabilistic rules on each of 15 Android apps' facts: every tuple of the derived relations.

groups.title: The ProbLog tutorial
groups.about: The programs of the ProbLog tutorial's pages that ask marginals (coins, Bayesian networks, dice, rule probabilities, higher-order predicates, inhibition effects, the tutorial's slides, Monty Hall, HMMs, PRISM-style programs, Bayesian dataflow and more), as the pages write them: each program's queries.
groups.source: the ProbLog tutorial (KU Leuven), written by gen_problogtut.py

groups.title: ProbLog's examples
groups.about: The example programs of ProbLog's repository, each with the answers its comments state: each program's queries.

groups.title: cplint's examples
groups.about: cplint's example programs written for PITA, read as LPADs: each program's queries.

groups.title: Three-sided die
groups.about: A three-sided die thrown until it shows 3: the probability that throw n shows 1, by n; cplint's example asks throws 0 to 3.
groups.source: Riguzzi and Swift (ICLP 2010, Fig. 3), cplint's threesideddice.pl, written by gen_threedie.py and gen_cplint.py

groups.title: A grammar, by its stack
groups.about: The ProbLog tutorial's probabilistic context-free grammar of balanced words, each choice identified by the state of the derivation: how the derivation of a word of length n starts, given the word, by n.
groups.source: the ProbLog tutorial's PCFG page, its second program, written by gen_pcfg.py

groups.title: An HMM of DNA
groups.about: A hidden Markov model of DNA sequences whose every choice is indexed by the states before it: the probability that it emits a given sequence of length n, by n.
groups.source: Christiansen and Gallagher (ICLP 2009) as PITA's evaluation runs it (Riguzzi and Swift, TPLP 2011), cplint's hmm.pl, written by gen_dnahmm.py

groups.title: A left-corner grammar
groups.about: A shift-reduce parser of a probabilistic grammar whose every choice is indexed by the derivation so far: the probability of a word of n letters, by n.
groups.source: Sato, Kameya and Kurihara (AMAI 2008), cplint's plcg.pl, written by gen_plcg.py

groups.title: Part-of-speech tagging
groups.about: A hidden Markov model of part-of-speech tags whose every choice is indexed by the tags before it: the probability of a sentence of five words said k times, by k.
groups.source: Lager's model as cplint's hmmpos.pl adapts it (Riguzzi), written by gen_hmmpos.py

groups.title: Handwritten formulas
groups.about: DeepProbLog's handwritten formulas of n symbols, each image's classifier an annotated disjunction and the formula parsed from its symbols: the probability of its label, by n.
groups.source: Manhaeve et al. (Artificial Intelligence 2021), written by gen_hwf.py

groups.title: Probabilistic grid
groups.about: An n x n grid with an edge of probability 0.5 from each node to its right, lower and lower-right neighbours: the probability of a path to the far corner from the node d steps before it on the diagonal, by n and d.
groups.source: ProbLog2's evaluation (Fierens et al., TPLP 2015, Section 9), written by gen_pgrid.py

losses: Where others win: ProbLog answers 1 of its tutorial's 115 programs that tddlog does not: numberguessing_1, which uses ProbLog's subquery/3.

categories.title: Probabilistic databases

groups.title: Queries QW and Q9
groups.about: The safe queries QW and Q9 over a complete tuple-independent database of N constants, whose lineage has no small decision-DNNF, by N.
groups.source: Beame et al. (ACM TODS 2017), written by gen_liftsep.py

groups.title: Paths of two edges
groups.about: Whether a random graph on N nodes, a tuple-independent table of its edges, has a path of two edges (#P-hard), by N.
groups.source: Fink et al. (VLDB J. 2013), written by gen_rgraph.py

groups.title: Queries h0 and h1
groups.about: The Boolean queries h0 and h1 (#P-hard) and a safe one over a tuple-independent database of n constants with two random S tuples each, by n.
groups.source: Dalvi and Suciu (VLDB J. 2007), written by gen_pdb.py

categories.title: Bayesian networks

groups.title: bnlearn's networks
groups.about: The networks of the bnlearn repository, every leaf queried, and with half the leaves observed and the rest queried; the large ones (barley, diabetes, mildew, munin1 to munin4) of the flip-hoisting evaluation; Roulette's nine and noDice's five networks of the same names, each asked for one variable (noDice's survey and water ask Roulette's, one instance each); and Ace's copies of hailfinder and pigs, the same tables, with one of Ace's evidence sets: the unobserved leaves.
groups.source: the bnlearn repository; Cheng et al. (PROBPROG 2021); the artifacts of Roulette (PLDI 2025) and noDice (OOPSLA 2026); Ace's benchmarks (Chavira and Darwiche)

groups.title: Ace's networks
groups.about: Ace's copies of alarm, diabetes, mildew, munin1 to munin4, pathfinder and water, each with one of the archive's evidence sets: the unobserved leaves. Not bnlearn's files: some tables in percent or as weights, munin1, munin3 and munin4 with three variables more, alarm's variables renamed.

groups.title: Promedus
groups.about: The Promedus diagnosis networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition: the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Pedigrees
groups.about: The pedigree networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition: the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Noisy-or networks
groups.about: BN2O networks after QMR-DT: d diseases, f findings with three noisy-or causes each and a leak, every finding observed: every disease, by d and f.
groups.source: the UAI 2008 evaluation, written by gen_noisyor.py

groups.title: Promedas noisy-or chains
groups.about: The or_chain networks (Promedas medical diagnosis networks, noisy-or chains) of the UAI 2022 inference competition's final PR set and of Ihler's collection: the partition function given the evidence.
groups.source: UAI 2022 inference competition (final PR set); Ihler's UAI model collection

groups.title: UAI 2006 networks
groups.about: The Bayesian networks of the UAI 2006 evaluation (named BN), in the UAI 2022 inference competition's final PR set and in Ihler's collection: the partition function given the evidence.
groups.source: UAI 2022 inference competition (final PR set); Ihler's UAI model collection

groups.title: Classic networks
groups.about: The classic networks of Ihler's collection (alarm, andes, barley, cpcs54, diabetes, hepar2, link, mildew, munin1, munin2, tcc4e and others): the partition function given the evidence.

groups.title: Mastermind
groups.about: The mastermind networks of Ace's benchmark archive, each with one of its evidence sets (the unobserved leaves), and of the UAI 2022 inference competition's final PR set (the partition function given the evidence).
groups.source: Ace's benchmarks (Chavira and Darwiche); UAI 2022 inference competition

groups.title: Blockmap
groups.about: The blockmap networks of Ace's benchmark archive, each with one of its evidence sets (the unobserved leaves), and of the UAI 2022 inference competition's final PR set (the partition function given the evidence).
groups.source: Ace's benchmarks (Chavira and Darwiche); UAI 2022 inference competition

groups.title: Friends and smokers
groups.about: The fs (friends and smokers) networks of Ace's benchmark archive, its one evidence set observed (every other variable), and of the UAI 2022 inference competition's final PR set (the partition function given the evidence).
groups.source: Ace's benchmarks (Chavira and Darwiche); UAI 2022 inference competition

groups.title: Students
groups.about: The students network of Ace's benchmark archive, with one of its evidence sets: the unobserved leaves.

losses: Where others win: the networks named BN of Ihler's collection. tddlog runs out of time on seven that pyAgrum or Merlin answers in 0.3 to 2.1 s, and on 20 more Merlin, pyAgrum or TensorInference.jl is at least twice as fast, up to 0.3 s against tddlog's 204 s.

categories.title: Markov networks

groups.title: Object detection
groups.about: The ObjectDetection networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition: the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Grids
groups.about: The Grids networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition: the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set); and the 20x20 grids of Ihler's collection: the partition function given the evidence.

groups.title: Image segmentation
groups.about: The Segmentation networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition: the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Dynamic Bayesian networks
groups.about: The DBN networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition (dynamic Bayesian networks): the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Constraint satisfaction problems
groups.about: The CSP networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition (constraint satisfaction problems): the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Markov logic networks
groups.about: The Alchemy networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition (Markov logic networks that Alchemy grounded): the marginals given the evidence (the UAI 2022 MAR tuning set) and the partition function (its PR tuning set).

groups.title: Protein side chains
groups.about: The protein side-chain networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition, named by PDB code: the partition function given the evidence.

groups.title: Binary pairwise networks
groups.about: The rus networks of the UAI 2022 inference competition, binary pairwise Markov networks of 854 variables and about 17,000 factors: the partition function given the evidence.

groups.title: Weighted CSPs
groups.about: The weighted constraint satisfaction problems of the UAI 2022 inference competition (myciel, queen, bwt3ac): the partition function given the evidence.

groups.title: Pedigrees
groups.about: The pedigree networks whose factors are not conditional probability tables, of the UAI 2022 inference competition's final PR set and of Ihler's collection: the partition function given the evidence.
groups.source: UAI 2022 inference competition (final PR set); Ihler's UAI model collection

groups.title: Promedas noisy-or chains
groups.about: The or_chain networks (Promedas medical diagnosis networks, noisy-or chains) of Ihler's collection whose factors are not conditional probability tables: the partition function given the evidence.

losses: Where others win: six partition functions of the UAI 2022 final set, five of them protein networks, and Ihler's pedigree50 run out of time or memory. TensorInference.jl answers the six in 12 to 45 s and pedigree50 in 133 s.

groups.title: Caesar cipher, 4 letters
groups.about: A key of 4 letters, letters drawn 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8 and added to the key modulo 4, one ciphertext letter observed k times: the key's distribution, by k.

groups.title: Caesar cipher, 32 letters
groups.about: A key of 32 letters, letters drawn from a nearly uniform table and added to the key modulo 32, one ciphertext letter observed k times: the key's distribution, by k.

groups.title: Caesar cipher, 26 letters
groups.about: A key of 26 letters, English letter frequencies, modulo 26, a fixed ciphertext of increasing length: the key's distribution, by the length.

groups.title: Caesar cipher, noisy
groups.about: A key of 26 letters, English letter frequencies, added to the key as 32-bit vectors, each letter observed as its encryption or, with probability 0.0001, as itself, n random ciphertext letters: the key's distribution, by n.

groups.title: Diamonds
groups.about: The Dice paper's network verification benchmark of diamonds in a row (gen_diamond of dicebench), by the number of diamonds: the paper's Dice program, Roulette's diamond.rkt, and one ProbLog program.

groups.title: Ladders
groups.about: The Dice paper's network verification benchmark of ladders (gen_ladder of dicebench), by the number of rungs: the paper's Dice program, Roulette's ladder.rkt, and one ProbLog program.

groups.title: Lossy network
groups.about: The lossy network of the Roulette paper: the distribution of the message received, a lost one included, by size.

groups.title: Router grid, failing links
groups.about: An N by N grid of routers whose links each work with probability 0.5: the probability that a packet from the top-left router reaches the bottom-right one, by N.
groups.source: Geni (ICFP 2025), Figure 11, after Fierens et al.'s grid

groups.title: Router grid, failing routers
groups.about: An N by N grid of routers that each work with a probability that depends on their left and upper neighbours: the probability that the bottom-right router works, by N.

groups.title: Weather factory
groups.about: The probability that all n factories are on strike within h days, by n at 10 days and by h with 10 factories.
groups.source: Rubicon's translation (Holtzen et al., CAV 2021), as Geni's evaluation runs it (ICFP 2025, Figure 9)

groups.title: Markov chain
groups.about: The motivating Markov chain of the Roulette paper, by its number of steps.

groups.title: Hidden Markov model
groups.about: Roulette's hidden Markov model under five questions (filtering and smoothing, marginal and joint, and the marginal likelihood), by length.

groups.title: Pluck's hidden Markov model
groups.about: Pluck's hidden Markov model of 50 steps, its own transitions and emissions: the probability of a sequence of observations.

groups.title: Sequence models
groups.about: Pluck's sequence models on inductive types: a PCFG of 23 terminals, string editing of 4 to 5 characters and sorted list generation of 8 elements.

groups.title: Contract signing, 40 components
groups.about: A contract signing protocol as a guarded-command step over 40 integer components (pmc1), iterated, by the number of steps.

groups.title: Contract signing, 24 components
groups.about: A contract signing protocol as a guarded-command step over 24 integer components (pmc2), iterated, by the number of steps.

groups.title: Perturbed-memory interpreter
groups.about: The Roulette paper's interpreter whose memory is perturbed: the distribution of its result, a run out of fuel included, by fuel with cells of 2 bits, and over three steps of fuel by the bit width of its cells, up to 10^8 bits.

groups.title: Integer arithmetic
groups.about: Cao et al.'s integer programs other than caesar (book, disease, fw, gcd, linext, luhn, plankton, radar, ranking, triangle and tugofwar), integers of 2 to 20 bits, at the sizes of the paper's Table 1: the distribution of each program's value.

groups.title: Coupon collector
groups.about: N rounds that each draw two coupons uniformly, observing that they differ: the probability that every coupon is held at the end, by N.

groups.title: 3-SAT
groups.about: SATLIB's uniform random 3-SAT formulas, ten of 20 variables and 91 clauses, uf50-0999 of 50 and 218, and 40 variables and 115 clauses of it: the probability that a uniform assignment satisfies each.

groups.title: Bounded retransmission
groups.about: The bounded retransmission protocol: N frames, each sent up to three times over a lossy channel and acknowledged over another: the probability that every frame is acknowledged, by N.

groups.title: Small Dice programs
groups.about: The small programs of the Dice paper's comparison with Psi and WebPPL (alarm, grass, noisy-or, two coins, murder mystery and two on evidence) and its naive Bayes digit classifier.

groups.title: Fault analysis of netlists
groups.about: Circulette's netlists of digital circuits, as its authors wrote them or converted from its Verilog designs (rkt_of_verilog.py): the probability that a gate's faults make the outputs wrong, and the posterior of each single, pair and triple of faults given that failure.

groups.title: Ripple-carry adder (fault analysis)
groups.about: Circulette's fullAdder8.v, a ripple-carry adder, at N bits: its fault analysis, by N.

groups.title: Multiply-accumulate (fault analysis)
groups.about: Circulette's openfpga_mac_2.v, a multiply-accumulate unit, at a data width of N bits: its fault analysis, by N.
